intent.purpose: Give the sealed contract.spec artifact — the JSON file every Contract Studio session seals, one per spec version — one shape the judge, the Contracts app and the page all check it against, and make a spec's changes and breaks measured against a baseline the spec names itself: the last approved version of this contract, or the shipped code when none is approved.
nonGoals: It does not check a spec's document — the OpenAPI object, the JSON Schema or the .d.ts text — which is the kind's own checks' job
It does not record which versions a person approved; that is the session's approval records
It does not cover the Contracts app's HTTP routes; the approved Contracts app API does
Judging intent per guarantee instead of over the whole intent is the follow-up this shape enables
It does not shape contract comments, map diagram groups, change summaries, or per-definition summaries
intent.audience: The Contract Studio sessions that seal specs, and the code and pages that read them back: the contract judge, the Contracts app, and the Contracts page.
consumers: The Contracts app that serves specs to the page (repo/packages/contracts/src/app.ts)
The Contracts page: Studio, RestView, ChangeList, and the web's local copy of the type (repo/packages/web/src/extensions/contracts/)
Recorded-session replay, which reads older specs sealed before this version
guarantees: A spec missing kind, title, version, intent, document or choices fails the shape: the root names all six in required
A decision is never left uncited: every choice carries at least one why, and every why names its source, its text and its ref
A break is never left unnamed: every breaking entry names at least one caller and holds one field, migration, that states how its callers keep working
A reader never rejects a spec for a field it does not know: every object in the shape allows unknown properties, so specs sealed under older names still read
A spec's changes and breaks are measured against the top-level baseline it names: the approved version number, or 'shipped'
A spec is never measured against an unapproved draft: a rejected draft is not a baseline
Entries a revision adds or changes, and every entry with no baseline, or 'shipped', are each one checkable fact: a stable id, text of at most 160 characters
An entry whose text equals a baseline entry's keeps that entry's id; renaming it fails the facts gate
A stored string entry stays valid, however long
The seal gate, the Intent type and the web's copy of it move in the code fix after this approval, so an id'd entry seals from that code on
The one-fact rule is a no-model gate: code checks the ids, the limit and the changes rows' facts, not the judge's reading

document.description: The sealed contract.spec artifact: one JSON file per spec version, written to artifacts/spec.json by a Contract Studio session and sealed into the session's catalog. This shape describes specs sealed from the approved version of this contract on; validateSpec runs only at seal time, so stored specs are never re-validated, and readers — the Contracts page, the Contracts app, the judge — keep tolerating specs sealed before it: without a baseline, without a migration on their breaking entries, and with the stray field names some carry. Measured against the version-1 document, 245 sealed contract.spec versions across 31 contract sessions on prod stand as 235 pass and 10 fail, all 10 of them version-1 drafts the gate never ran laterVersionProblems on, in pairs from 5 sessions (20207648, ea66d629, 69e5aecf, 6fe21e34, aab002bf). Some stored version-1 drafts do not satisfy this shape, and readers must tolerate them: 34 breaking entries lack what (they say change instead), 8 carry callers as a string, and of the 526 breaking entries, 159 already carry migration while the stray fields are choice (50), change (18), was (16), now (16), note (9) and why (4).

kind.description: The kind of the contract; picks which standard document `document` holds and which guide, checks and diff apply to it.

title.description: The name of the contract, shown on the Contracts page and in the approval ask.

version.description: The spec's own version, as the gate applies it: one more than the last delivered — gate-passed — spec version. A proposal the reviewer rejects still consumes its number, and a failed revision reuses it, which is why approved versions skip numbers (deployment.json went v11 approved, v12 and v13 rejected, v14 approved). Approval does not affect numbering.

baseline.description: The baseline this version's `changes` and `compatibility` are measured against: the version number of this contract's last approved version, or "shipped" when no version is approved and the surface is already shipped to its callers. Absent when there is no baseline, which is only a greenfield surface nothing is shipped on; then `changes` and `compatibility` are absent too. The code requires the baseline, and with it the two sections, exactly when a baseline exists — at any version number against an approved version, from version 1 against a shipped surface — and never measures a version against an unapproved draft. No code can tell whether a surface is shipped, so the gate does not decide it: "shipped" is the author's claim, checked by the reviewer against the cited code, and the gate checks only that a named approved version exists when baseline is a number.

intent.description: What the contract is for, in one place a judge can check the document against.

document.description: The kind's standard document: an OpenAPI 3.1 object for rest, a JSON Schema 2020-12 schema for json-schema, or the .d.ts source text for typescript. Its soundness is the kind's own checks' job, not this shape's.

choices.description: Every decision the document rests on, in at least one row; the document must not outgrow the list.

changes.description: What this version changes from the baseline named in `baseline`, one row per choice it revises; never measured against an unapproved draft of this contract. Present, together with `compatibility`, exactly when a baseline exists.

compatibility.description: What this version breaks and what it keeps, checked in code against the baseline named in `baseline`. Present, together with `changes`, exactly when a baseline exists.

breaking.description: Every break the version makes to the baseline, one entry per break, each naming the callers it hurts and stating one migration; empty when the version breaks nothing.

safe.description: What stays working for the contract's callers against the baseline, each checked in code; empty when there is nothing to report.

intent.description: What the contract is for, in one place a judge can check the document against.

purpose.description: What the contract makes possible or safe, in plain words.

nonGoals.description: What the contract deliberately does not cover, so a decision that drifts there is visible; may be empty. An entry is one checkable fact, by the same rule as guarantees.

audience.description: Who the contract is for in plain words: the people and programs it governs.

consumers.description: The programs and pages that read the contract and must keep working, each named; may be empty.

guarantees.description: What the contract promises its consumers; each promise has a mechanism in the document that keeps it. An entry is one checkable fact: a stored string that stays valid until a revision changes it, or an object with a stable id and text of at most 160 characters. An entry a revision adds or changes must be the id'd object within the limit, and a spec with no baseline, or with a baseline of 'shipped', must have every entry id'd.

choice.description: One decision the spec rests on, and every reason behind it.

id.description: A stable slug naming the decision; rows of `changes` refer back to it.

pointer.description: A JSON pointer into `document` the decision governs; empty when the decision is spec-wide.

decision.description: What was decided, in one sentence.

why.description: Every reason behind the decision, in at least one entry.
One reason a decision was made, citing where the reason comes from.

source.description: Where the reason comes from: an answer the person gave, a rule of the kind's authoring guide, or a line of code.

text.description: The reason in plain words; for a code source, what the cited line shows.

ref.description: The thing cited: the question as asked or its id, the person's first description as "request", a guide heading, or a path:line in the session's workspace.

change.description: One row of `changes`: what the baseline had, what this version has instead, and why.

choice.description: The id of the choice in `choices` this row revises.

was.description: What the baseline had for that choice, in a short phrase.

now.description: What this version has for that choice, in a short phrase.

why.description: Why the change was made: the request, answer or requirement it answers.

facts.description: The ids of the facts this row adds, changes or removes; required by the gate whenever the revision touches either list.

breaking.description: One break to the baseline: what stops working for callers, who it hurts, and the one change that fixes it.

what.description: The break in one sentence: what the baseline let a caller do that this version no longer does.

callers.description: The callers the break hurts, each named: the code, page or session that reads the baseline shape, found by reading the code that calls the contract.

migration.description: The one change each named caller makes to keep working; required on every breaking entry of a spec sealed from this version on. Readers keep tolerating the stored entries without it, some of which state the same under the stray names `change` and `choice`.

fact.description: One entry of intent.guarantees or intent.nonGoals: one checkable fact, as a stored string or as an id'd object.

factEntry.$comment: The judge's facts_decomposed gate fails each offending entry with: facts are not decomposed: {location}: {reason}, so {fix}. {location} is {list}[{index}], or (id '{id}'), or changes[{row}].facts when there is no list index, as with a removed id. {reason} is one of: over 160 — the text is {n} characters, so split it into one fact per entry; no id — give it one; bad id — '{id}' is not lowercase dotted or dashed, so rename it; duplicate id — '{id}' is used more than once, so give each entry its own id; renamed id — the text matches the baseline's id '{id}', so keep that id; id named in no changes row's facts — '{id}' was added with new text, changed or removed, so name it in the row that touches the list; facts id the revision did not touch — '{id}' was named but was neither added, changed nor removed, and is not an id given to unchanged text, so remove it from facts.

id.description: A stable id naming the fact: lowercase letters and digits with dots or dashes, beginning with a letter, unique within the spec across guarantees and nonGoals, kept across versions while the fact stays the same fact.

text.description: The one fact in plain words, at most 160 characters: one sentence one meaning, too short for a second fact.

factEntry.description: One checkable fact: a stable id, kept while the fact stays the same fact, and its text of at most 160 characters.
